objective: Owner request 2026-10-02 12:45 UTC: use real-time prediction-market odds (Polymarket/Kalshi) for decisions, factors or strategies and iterate. First mechanism tested: prediction-market-implied uncertainty about scheduled macro releases (CPI, payrolls, GDP, PCE; FOMC reported separately) as the conditioning variable for the equity macro-announcement premium; second, conditional on free consensus data, the Kalshi-minus-consensus expectation gap as a predictor of the release reaction. Plus an hourly point-in-time forward collector that runs regardless of the backtest result.
target_regime_and_horizon: Event horizon: one session (T-1 close to T close, and T-1 close to T open). Samples: full Kalshi history (first valid event in 2021-09/2022 .. 2026-09-17) and the anchor window 2024-01-08 .. 2026-09-17. There is no pre-2021 stress window because the data do not exist; the literature (Ai/Bansal/Guo 2023 Table 1, 1961-2023) is the long-run prior. Applicable regime: periods of elevated macro and policy uncertainty, as in 2022-2026 (Jan 2020 - Aug 2023 premium 16.33 bp per announcement vs 10.68 bp long-run). Failure signal: rolling 24-event D turns negative.
existing_solution_comparison: Published: the announcement premium itself (Savor-Wilson 2013; Ai-Bansal-Guo NBER w31923, 1961-2023: 10.68 bp/day on announcement days, t 5.36, vs 0.93 bp; non-FOMC 8.65 bp, t 3.71) and option- or variance-based predictors of FOMC announcement returns (Hu-Pan-Wang-Zhu JFE 2022; Jacobs-Ke-Pan 2022; Liu-Tang-Zhou 2022, R2 7.51%; Gafka-Savor-Wilson 2021 realized variance). Missing: release-specific uncertainty for non-FOMC releases (payrolls, CPI, GDP) for which no options exist; FEDS 2026-010 (Diercks-Katz-Wright) shows Kalshi supplies exactly these distributions, well-behaved and news-responsive, but tests forecasting accuracy, not asset returns. Reused, not rebuilt: WillBtK/macro_kalshi (MIT) distribution construction (middle-out monotone cleaning of threshold markets). No public product or replication links Kalshi/Polymarket-implied release uncertainty to the announcement premium (searched 2026-10-02, see queries).
remaining_evidence_gap: Unknown before this step: (1) whether the announcement premium exists in 2021-2026 for CPI/payrolls/GDP days on QQQ/SPY/IWM (the FOMC drift was already refuted locally); (2) whether Kalshi-implied variance measures uncertainty rather than illiquidity of tail strikes; (3) whether the premium scales with it; (4) whether a free point-in-time consensus history exists for H2.
negative_experiments_checked: dir:prediction_market_crypto_as_equity_signal (evidence_too_weak 2026-09-23; generic odds-to-equity lead-lag; this iteration does not reopen it, the mechanism here is risk compensation for scheduled uncertainty, not lead-lag). dir:pre_fomc_announcement_drift (refuted, H-20260928-05: FOMC_DRIFT_SPY anchor Sharpe -0.84, FOMC_DRIFT_TQQQ 0.31): FOMC days are reported separately and excluded from the primary statistic. dir:crypto_weekend_to_monday_equity_transmission (refuted 2026-09-29: priced in the gap) -- shows that information available before the fill tends to be in the open; hence R_co is reported next to R_cc. Amburgey arXiv 2504.02731: sector stocks react to election-odds shocks contemporaneously, not with a lag (supports not testing lead-lag here). ForesightFlow arXiv 2605.00493: documented insider cases are deadline-resolved markets with no link to traded assets (out of scope).
cost_and_execution_assumptions: MOC entry at T-1 (signal known by 15:00 ET, before the 15:50 ET MOC cutoff), exit MOC at T (R_cc) or MOO at T (R_co). Costs per side: QQQ/SPY/TLT 2 bp, IWM 3 bp, TQQQ 5 bp; stress = double. TLT short borrow 0.5%/yr pro rata (easy to borrow). Long-only QQQ/SPY/IWM/TQQQ need no borrow. Invested on about 6-10% of sessions, so it is judged as a program overlay at 0.25x (0.5x if Reg T allows) equity notional, not as a standalone sleeve.
stop_condition: H1 continues only if D = mean(QQQ R_cc | U_rel>1) - mean(QQQ R_cc | U_rel<=1) on non-FOMC release days is >= +15 bp with permutation p <= 0.10 (1000 within-series shuffles, seed 20261002) in the full sample and > 0 in the anchor sample. D < +5 bp or wrong-signed in the full sample: H1 refuted, candidates not scored for adoption. H2 runs only if a free point-in-time consensus history passes feasibility; otherwise blocked_data.

sources.claim: Kalshi distributions for FOMC, CPI, core CPI, PCE, unemployment, payrolls, GDP, recession are well-behaved and respond sharply to news; variance of the fed funds distribution falls after data releases (2022-2025); Kalshi mode matched every FOMC decision on the day before since 2022 (significantly better than fed funds futures); headline CPI forecasts significantly better than the Bloomberg consensus; core CPI and unemployment similar to consensus. No asset-return test.
sources.market_and_period: Kalshi event markets on FOMC decisions, CPI, core CPI, PCE, unemployment, payrolls, GDP and recession, mostly 2022-2025; Federal Reserve Board FEDS 2026-010 (also NBER w34702).
sources.applicability: Direct basis of the data and mechanism: Kalshi distributions are well-behaved, respond to news and their variance falls after releases, so the standard deviation of the distribution the afternoon before a release is a usable release-specific uncertainty measure. No asset-return result, which is what this iteration tests.
sources.limitations: Text extracted from the PDF by the lead (not publisher HTML). Tests forecast accuracy and news response of the distributions, not equity returns; early Kalshi years are thin and tail strikes can be stale; a Kalshi series is not a consensus survey.
sources.independent_replication: No independent replication of the forecasting claims found; the MIT fork WillBtK/macro_kalshi rebuilds the distribution construction from the same replication package.

sources.claim: 1961-2023: 10.68 bp/day excess return on announcement days (FOMC, payrolls, GDP, ISM, earlier of CPI/PPI; t 5.36) vs 0.93 bp otherwise; FOMC 17.61 bp, non-FOMC 8.65 bp (t 3.71); Jan 2020-Aug 2023 16.33 bp per announcement; FOMC premium low 2016-2019 (Kurov-Wolfe-Gilbert 2021). Reviews evidence that pre-announcement uncertainty (Hu-Pan-Wang-Zhu 2022), option-implied volatility (Jacobs-Ke-Pan 2022; Liu-Tang-Zhou 2022 R2 7.51%) and realized variance (Gafka-Savor-Wilson 2021) predict announcement returns; counter-evidence Zhang-Zhao 2022 (premium low when information uncertainty is high).
sources.market_and_period: US equity market excess returns 1961-2023 on FOMC, payrolls, GDP, ISM and CPI/PPI announcement days; NBER Working Paper 31923, November 2023, revised December 2023 (day of month not stated, 01 used).
sources.applicability: Gives the prior that announcement days carry a premium (non-FOMC 8.65 bp, t 3.71) that was larger in 2020-2023 and reviews predictors of it (pre-announcement uncertainty, option-implied and realized variance). The iteration tests whether a prediction-market uncertainty measure scales it.
sources.limitations: Working paper, index-level returns net of no trading costs; premium in 2021-2026 is unknown and the 2016-2019 FOMC premium was low; evidence that premium scales with uncertainty is mixed (Zhang-Zhao 2022 find the opposite for information uncertainty).
sources.independent_replication: The announcement premium is replicated across papers (Savor-Wilson 2013, Lucca-Moench 2015 for FOMC); its scaling with uncertainty has several supporting studies but no consensus.

sources.claim: MIT-licensed fork of the FEDS replication package: Kalshi series KXFED, KXCPIYOY, KXCPICOREYOY, KXCPI, KXACPI, KXU3, KXGDP, KXGDPYEAR, KXPAYROLLS; public candlesticks; middle-out no-arbitrage cleaning of threshold CDFs.
sources.market_and_period: GitHub repository (README snapshot; last commit 2026-08-28), Kalshi series KXFED, KXCPI, KXPAYROLLS, KXGDP, KXU3 and others, daily distributions 2021-2026.
sources.applicability: Source of the middle-out monotone cleaning and of the series and threshold conventions; code is ported (credited in the docstring) rather than rebuilt.
sources.limitations: Fork maintained by one person; an R pipeline with a daily, not hourly, grid and a trade-level path; consensus data are not in the repository. Our code reimplements the cleaning in Python and is tested on synthetic candles only.
sources.independent_replication: Fork of the Diercks-Katz-Wright replication package; the README documents the cleaning but no independent validation was found.

sources.claim: High-frequency election-probability shocks move energy, defense and clean-energy stocks contemporaneously; no measurable lag (evidence against odds-to-equity lead-lag).
sources.market_and_period: US sector stock indices around US presidential election-probability shocks, high-frequency identification; arXiv 2504.02731 v1 3 Apr 2025, v2 15 Jun 2025.
sources.applicability: Evidence that equities react to prediction-market probability shocks contemporaneously, so a lead-lag use of odds is not supported; this iteration therefore tests a risk-compensation mechanism instead and keeps the lead-lag row evidence_too_weak.
sources.limitations: Single working paper, election shocks only, sector indices; says nothing about scheduled macro releases.

sources.claim: Polymarket-focused dataset suite from October 2020: more than 3.29M market records, over 1.90B order execution records, nearly 21M oracle events; the paper demonstrates CPI expectation reconstruction for economists.
sources.market_and_period: Polymarket-focused dataset suite October 2020 to date; arXiv 2604.20421 v1 22 Apr 2026, v2 25 Sep 2026.

sources.claim: Information Leakage Score framework on a 911,237-market Polymarket corpus; the publicly documented insider cases are systematically deadline-resolved (0 of 24 FFIC inventory markets satisfy the original scope conditions); the abstract links them to no traded financial asset.
sources.market_and_period: 911,237-market Polymarket corpus; arXiv 2605.00493 v1 1 May 2026, v2 14 May 2026.
sources.applicability: Shows the documented informed-trading cases on Polymarket are deadline-resolved markets with no tie to traded financial assets, so they give no basis for an odds-to-equity signal; keeps that use out of scope.
sources.limitations: Pilot evaluation of a leakage-score method; the abstract links the cases to no traded asset and says nothing about macro-release markets.
sources.independent_replication: No independent replication; companion paper cited but not read.

cheapest_decisive_test.action: After the manifest is frozen and pre-backtest validation passes: one script computes U_rel per event from Kalshi hourly candles (signal candle ending <= 15:00 ET on T-1), joins SIP daily QQQ/SPY/IWM/TLT returns, and writes the H0 table, the H1 statistic D with a 1000-shuffle permutation p, the T+1 and random-session placebos, and the 9 candidates' per-event stats.
cheapest_decisive_test.pass_condition: D >= +15 bp, permutation p <= 0.10 in the full sample, and D > 0 in the anchor sample (QQQ, R_cc, non-FOMC release days).
cheapest_decisive_test.falsification_condition: D < +5 bp or wrong-signed in the full sample: H1 refuted; the registry gets a new row dir:prediction_market_macro_release_uncertainty_premium marked refuted with the numbers.
